rules: Preserve user and supporting-document facts verbatim where precision matters.
Label architect-selected components and targets as proposed.
Express material unknowns as open clarifications; never silently default them into commitments.
Do not invent customer facts, achieved benefits, approvals, contacts, dates, prices, volumes, user counts, regulations, or SLAs.

document_basis.description: Make the SOW reviewable and auditable.
rules: Keep document control to title, customer, version and date; keep provenance internal.
For POC-to-production, distinguish POC evidence from proposed production requirements.
Ask only unanswered decisions that block scope, sizing, price or acceptance; omit routine discovery questions.

scope_definition.description: Define a bounded, testable work package.
rules: State current state, target outcome, in-scope capabilities, exclusions, dependencies, assumptions, deliverables, and acceptance evidence.
Group implementation actions into cohesive modules; do not manufacture tracking IDs or per-feature evidence rows.
Do not include deliverables that conflict with Out of Scope.
Use change control for additions to the approved baseline.

architecture.description: Require design rationale without pretending a diagram exists.
rules: Describe logical components, end-to-end flow, trust boundaries, deployment boundaries, controls, observability, and alternatives.
Map each proposed AWS service to a purpose and requirement.
Distinguish confirmed services from recommended services.
Address availability, scaling and cost only to the level supported by known requirements.
Document sources, owners, formats, classifications, volumes/status, access patterns, retention and deletion when known.
Document each integration's direction, interface, authentication, data, owner, frequency and status.
Do not estimate storage or throughput as a fact when usage is unknown.

security_privacy_compliance.description: Connect controls to requirements and evidence.
rules: Cover identity, secrets, encryption, network boundaries, audit/logging, vulnerability management, privacy and incident response as applicable.
Name a compliance framework only when the source confirms it.
State owner and verification evidence for each material control.

non_functional_requirements.description: Keep performance and reliability measurable and honest.
rules: Capture latency, throughput, concurrency, availability, RTO, RPO, retention and capacity when provided.
Leave absent values blank; do not invent test targets or SLAs.
Specify measurement method, environment, workload and test window.

testing_and_traceability.description: Link requirements to evidence and acceptance.
rules: Define environments, test data, functional, integration, regression, performance, security and UAT approaches as applicable.
For AI/data quality, define benchmark set, scoring method, sampling, reviewer role and evidence.
Group acceptance checks into distinct end-to-end outcomes; describe the shared test method once.
For POC-to-production, revalidate POC results under production-representative conditions.
Use a compact milestone plan with timeframe and outcome, not one phase per module.
Include review cycles, decision gates, testing, documentation and handover.
Label derived duration as a planning assumption and reconcile it across all sections.
Assign decision, dependency and escalation owner roles.
Use source-backed prices and funding status only.
When usage is unknown, use cost-driver ranges/basis and list variables required for a calculator baseline.
Reconcile resource loading with scope and schedule.
Leave unsupported implementation pricing or funding blank.
Include only project-specific risks with an actionable mitigation; do not generate a risk catalogue.
For production, define monitoring, incident model, runbooks, backup/recovery, patching, capacity/cost, change and service review.
Distinguish included hypercare from ongoing support requiring a separate agreement.
Use stable terminology, concise prose, meaningful headings and tables only for comparable records.
Avoid repetition, marketing filler, vague promises, fake precision and unresolved template placeholders.
Ensure legal/admin sections contain no stale named contacts or pre-approved marketing permission.
